observation: Existing LLM-based multi-agent systems can handle simple dialogue tasks, but complex tasks remain difficult because naively chaining LLMs induces cascading hallucinations and logic inconsistencies. Real-world LLM agent frameworks tend to oversimplify the complexities of collaborative problem solving and often rely on unstructured natural-language dialogue, which loses information across rounds and produces unproductive chatter. Existing code-generation methods also lack self-correction mechanisms that verify runtime executability, leaving complex software engineering tasks unmet.

claims: A prevalent strategy for using LLMs on complex goals is to orchestrate multiple agents with specialized roles and let them solve a problem through conversational turn-taking.
Role-specialized multi-agent LLM systems have been shown to carry out software-development pipelines that include analysis, implementation, and testing on small tasks.

MetaGPT motivates its design by observing that relying solely on natural-language dialogue among agents induces cascading hallucinations, logic inconsistencies, and information loss, and therefore encodes intermediate products as structured artifacts and imposes standardized operating procedures on the collaboration.

claims: LLM agents are often organized as closed-loop reason-act systems that use environment observations, tool outputs, or human input to ground subsequent decisions.
Reflexive mechanisms augment such agents with revision from an episodic buffer or with a model's own critique and retry.

Controlled studies of self-correction have found that LLMs do not reliably correct their own answers using purely internal verbal feedback; improvement requires external verification signals such as oracle feedback or execution results.

claims: Large pretrained code generation models often achieve high accuracy by sampling many completions and then filtering or reranking them with execution on test cases.
Execution signals can also be injected back into the generator: teaching an LLM to debug its output from runtime error messages substantially improves code generation and repair.
The code-generation line of work is therefore able to verify runtime behavior, but only at the granularity of a single standalone program with a predetermined executable test harness.

claims: Function-level coding benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP consist of self-contained short programs, so test-based sampling and reranking is an effective and dominant methodology.
Repository-scale benchmarks such as SWE-bench ask models to resolve real-world GitHub issues by editing full code bases, and initial LLM-based agents solve only a small fraction of the instances.

Complex software-engineering collaboration consequently remains unresolved by existing code-generation techniques, which lack a structured multi-agent workflow with executable verification at each step.
